source_text: Omnibus licet membris lauet quotidie Israel, numquam tamen mundus est. certe manus eius semper inmundae, sanguine prophetarum et ipsius domini incrustatae in aeternum; et ideo conscientia patrum hereditarii rei nec attollere eas ad dominum audent, ne exclamet aliquis Eseias, ne exhorreat Christus. nos uero non attollimus tantum, sed etiam expandimus, et dominicam passionem modulantes et orantes confitemur Christo.
thought_title: Israel's unclean hands versus Christian hands spread in confession of Christ
orientation: Tertullian is contrasting the perpetual uncleanness of Israel's hands, stained by the blood of the prophets and the Lord, with the Christian practice of lifting and spreading the hands in prayer.
pass_a_gloss: Although Israel may wash all its limbs daily, it is nevertheless never clean. Certainly its hands are always unclean, encrusted forever with the blood of the prophets and of the Lord himself; and therefore, as hereditary guilty ones by the conscience of the fathers, they do not dare even to lift them to the Lord, lest some Isaiah cry out, lest Christ shudder. But we not only lift them, but even spread them out, and, singing the Lord's passion and praying, we confess to Christ.

choices.why: The verb conveys a hardened, caked-on stain that remains permanently, matching the image of blood that cannot be washed off.
The phrase means they are guilty by inheritance, carrying the guilt of their fathers; 'hereditary guilty ones' preserves the noun force of 'rei' and the adjective's causal sense.
The verb means to sing or chant in measured rhythm; 'singing' keeps the musical sense of the Latin participle.
The dative 'Christo' indicates the one to whom confession is made; the verb here carries the sense of open acknowledgment in prayer.
'Exhorreat' conveys a strong physical recoil of horror; 'shudder' captures that visceral reaction.

bible_refs.note: The reference to Isaiah crying out against hands full of blood echoes Isaiah 1:15, where God says he will not listen because their hands are full of blood.

pass_b_english: Israel may wash every limb every day, yet it is never clean. Its hands are certainly always unclean, encrusted forever with the blood of the prophets and of the Lord himself. For that reason, as hereditary guilty ones by the conscience of their fathers, they do not dare even to lift their hands to the Lord, lest some Isaiah cry out, lest Christ shudder. But we not only lift our hands—we spread them out—and as we sing of the Lord's passion and pray, we confess to Christ.
